subject: Acme Health procurement: channel options, co-sell incentives, and invoicing
messages:
From: Sophia Chan <sophia.chan@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Health procurement: evaluating marketplace vs direct

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the Dedicated capacity option. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few practical questions so we can decide whether to route this through AWS Marketplace (or another cloud marketplace) or go straight to a direct contract/MSA with Redwood. High-level asks below: 

- For a 3-month pilot (small footprint) what’s the fastest procurement path to start? Marketplace listing or direct PO against an MSA?
- If we buy through AWS Marketplace, how do discounts and co-sell incentives work? Will Redwood still credit co-sell rebates to Acme?
- Billing & invoicing: marketplace invoices often go through AWS and take longer — what do you recommend if Acme needs standard net-30 vendor invoices vs marketplace billing?
- Contracting: can we sign a short MSA now and add a marketplace listing later (we need SOC 2 evidence and limited data residency notes)?

I attached Acme's PO template and the typical procurement checklist for your finance team. Could you respond with recommended routing + a suggested minimal set of docs we should send to Procurement/Legal?

Appreciate it,

Sophia Chan
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health
Sophia.chan@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme_PO_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophia Chan <sophia.chan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health procurement: evaluating marketplace vs direct

Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear list. High level guidance first, then I’ll attach the documents/legal checklist: 

1) Fastest path to start: AWS Marketplace (or GCP/Azure equivalent) typically gets you up fastest for a pilot because there’s no vendor onboarding/PO lag on our side — you can configure and access within a few business days once the listing is active. If Acme needs vendor invoices and PO processes that route through Accounts Payable, direct contract (PO against an MSA) provides the cleanest invoicing and is what we recommend for any multi-quarter committed purchase.

2) Discounts & co-sell: co-sell incentives are typically an add-on program managed between Redwood and the cloud partner. If you buy via the Marketplace listing, the purchase flows through the marketplace and the partner rebate/credit timing can vary (often quarterly). For direct contracts we can apply negotiated discounts directly on our invoices and reflect those in the SOW. We support passing partner credits through in many cases — we’ll confirm specifics for AWS once we check the co-sell intake for your account.

3) Billing & invoicing: Marketplace invoices are issued by the cloud provider (AWS) which can delay AP reconciliation; if Acme requires standard Redwood net-30 invoices to your AP system, the direct invoicing route is preferable. We also have a hybrid approach: start on marketplace for pilot, sign MSA, then move to direct invoicing for production.

4) Contracting & compliance: yes — we can sign a simple MSA now and publish a marketplace listing later. For SOC 2 and data residency, I’ve attached our SOC 2 summary and a short checklist of evidence we commonly provide. If you need more detailed reports we can route a secure share through our compliance portal.

Action items I suggest:
- I’ll attach our marketplace seller guide and a pricing grid that shows marketplace vs direct list prices.
- Laura (cc'd) will flag any co-sell promotions or credits we can commit to for the pilot.
- Vivek (cc'd) can advise on timing and partner intake for AWS co-sell.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm which path you want to take and what your AP team needs. Which time works for you?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_aws_marketplace_seller_guide.pdf, AWS_marketplace_pricing_grid.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Looping you both in — my quick take: for a narrow 3-month pilot I favor Marketplace (fast enablement + simpler trial billing), but we should offer a commitment-path that transitions to direct invoicing with a small committed discount. If Acme wants co-sell crediting to their team, we'll need to confirm the partner rebate mechanics with AWS (they're sometimes split across quarters).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1452334/rdw-acme-2027-03 — add notes about preference for marketplace pilot + MSA in parallel.

- Laura
Director, GTM Partnerships

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health procurement: evaluating marketplace vs direct

Thanks for the context — a few operational notes from my side: 

- AWS co-sell timeline: Marketplace listing + co-sell intake usually takes 2–3 weeks if there are no custom entitlements. The partner rebate/credit is tracked on the partner side and typically paid quarterly. We can confirm whether Redwood will assign any upfront invoice credit to Acme for pilot credits; that requires a partner rebate commitment we can negotiate with AWS.
- Direct contract path: we can execute a short-term MSA + SOW within 5–7 business days (legal review permitting) and issue net-30 invoices directly to Acme AP. For the commercial team, I recommend a 10% pilot discount if they commit to a 6–12 month renewal, or an equivalent marketplace co-sell credit if they prefer to buy via AWS.
- Compliance: SOC 2 summary is fine for initial procurement. For data residency (if they require EU or segmented storage) we’ll need to map to Private deployment or dedicated tenancy options — that’s more of an enterprise provisioning conversation.

I attached the latest MSA (MSA_redwood_v2.pdf) and an internal note on how we route co-sell credits for marketplace deals. For the HubSpot record, I’ll add an estimated co-sell credit line item and timeline.

Proposed commercial offer to Sophia (short and actionable):
1) Pilot: 3 months, Marketplace route for fast enablement, pilot pricing = list price less 10% pilot discount (or equivalent partner rebate applied later).
2) If production: transition to direct contract with negotiated committed discount and net-30 Redwood invoicing; Redwood to credit any confirmed partner rebate against future invoices on a reconciliation cadence.

I can join the call with Procurement if needed tomorrow morning.

-Vivek
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redwood_v2.pdf
